marketInfo.assetDescription:
Junior USDe (jrUSDe) is a yield-bearing investment product, representing the junior risk tranche in Strata’s structure. It provides leveraged upside to sUSDe APY while simultaneously functioning as a liquid insurance pool for srUSDe. By absorbing excess risk and volatility associated with sUSDe APY, jrUSDe earns a risk premium from the senior tranche, delivering potentially higher yields for risk-tolerant investors.

jrUSDe receives the residual yield after the senior tranche is paid and absorbs any shortfall when sUSDe APY falls below the guaranteed minimum yield for srUSDe tied to the benchmark rate (Supply-weighted average of USDC/USDT lending rates on Aave Core). As a result, jrUSDe outperforms sUSDe APY in high-yield environments but may underperform when sUSDe APY drops below the benchmark rate.

marketInfo.assetDescription: The Royco Junior Tranche for apyUSD represents a specialized high-yield market where risk-tolerant users provide "first-loss" liquidity to back apyUSD, a dividend-backed stablecoin. It provides higher yield by earning a risk premium for underwriting Senior protection but it takes losses first, up to the coverage % shown here.

conversionRate.toUnit: USD worth of apyUSD staked in Royco Junior Tranche

deposit.description: Native minting is available in the link attached

marketInfo.riskInvolved:
The Junior Tranche exchange rate is explicitly designed to fluctuate and can decrease substantially. Junior LPs are first-loss capital providers who earn enhanced yield in exchange for absorbing senior losses first. Potential Loss Scenarios:

  • Providing Coverage for Senior Losses - Whenever the underlying investment suffers a loss, junior capital is used first to make senior whole. Every dollar of senior loss (up to junior's total capacity) results in a direct dollar reduction in junior's value. This is the primary and expected mechanism by which junior can lose value.

  • Direct Junior Investment Losses - If the junior tranche has its own separate underlying investment (depending on the market configuration), losses in that investment directly reduce junior's value independent of any coverage provided to seniors.

  • Complete Wipeout Risk - In catastrophic loss scenarios, junior capital can be reduced to zero, meaning junior shareholders lose their entire investment. This occurs when senior losses exceed or equal the total junior capital.

  • Fixed-Term Lockup During Recovery - When junior provides coverage for senior losses, the market enters a temporary fixed-term state. During this period, Senior withdrawals and Junior deposits are blocked to protect existing juniors from realizing losses via coverage payouts and dilution respectively. The market waits for the fixed term to elapse or for the underlying to recover. If the fixed term ends without full recovery, the coverage losses become permanent.

(From Underlying Protocol)
